AI-assisted Skill (20%)The learner uses AI effectively as a tool rather than relying on it blindly.Examples:Writes a precise prompt such as “Generate Python code for computing homography using OpenCV with four pairs of matched points.”After AI provides code, the learner notices an error (e.g., wrong function arguments in cv2.findHomography).Adjusts AI code to run on their actual dataset (e.g., changing image paths, adapting for grayscale vs. color images, handling batch inputs).Simplifies redundant AI-generated code for better readability.4. Critical Thinking (10%)The learner goes beyond execution and reflects on results.Examples:Explains why homography fails when points are nearly collinear.Analyzes why edge detection produces too many false edges in noisy images.Points out that AI-generated code works only for synthetic data but not for real-world images.Suggests simple improvements such as applying Gaussian smoothing before edge detection, or using RANSAC to improve homography robustness.

Conceptual Understanding (20%)The learner demonstrates understanding of the underlying theory.Examples:Can explain what a homography is (a transformation mapping points between two planes).Understands the principle of edge detection (detecting intensity changes in the image).Explains why normalization is needed before feeding images into a neural network.If AI provides the code, the learner can rephrase and explain the method in their own words.3. AI-assisted Skill (20%)The learner uses AI effectively as a tool rather than relying on it blindly.Examples:Writes a precise prompt such as “Generate Python code for computing homography using OpenCV with four pairs of matched points.”After AI provides code, the learner notices an error (e.g., wrong function arguments in cv2.findHomography).Adjusts AI code to run on their actual dataset (e.g., changing image paths, adapting for grayscale vs. color images, handling batch inputs).Simplifies redundant AI-generated code for better readability.4. Critical Thinking (10%)The learner goes beyond execution and reflects on results.Examples:Explains why homography fails when points are nearly collinear.Analyzes why edge detection produces too many false edges in noisy images.Points out that AI-generated code works only for synthetic data but not for real-world images.Suggests simple improvements such as applying Gaussian smoothing before edge detection, or using RANSAC to improve homography robustness.

note: 1. On-going Assessment: 40% Students work in a project team of 4-5 members on the assignments as appointed by the teacher The works are organized by iterations with the contents and assessments as below (each student is assign to practice full-stack codes on assigned/selected function). Throughout the process, students are encouraged to use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot), under the following conditions: - Must transparently declare AI usage (e.g., what prompt was used, which part was generated by AI). - Must explain AI-generated output using their own understanding. a. Evaluation 1 (20%) – Requirement Analysis & Modeling Create use case descriptions and UML diagrams (static and dynamic models). AI can assist with modeling, but students must present their reasoning independently. Required Deliverables: AI prompts (if used), UML diagrams (e.g., PlantUML or Visio), written explanations. b. Evaluation 2 (20%) – Software Architecture & Design Design software architecture, decompose into subsystems, object-oriented design, and database schema. AI can help propose architecture or generate code samples, but students must refine and justify the result. Required Deliverables: Architecture docs, diagrams, code snippets, explanation of AI-assisted parts. 2. Final Project Presentation: 60% Each team presents their integrated software product and individual responsibilities. The individual evaluation includes an additional component for AI usage as follows: - Integrated Software Product Demostration for Software design (30%): Web API , Web Admin, Mobile App... - Mastery of assigned works: weighted 20% - Soft Skills & Working Attitudes: weighted 10% AI Evaluation Rubric (for individual performance – up to 10 points) - Understanding of AI Output - Customization and Enhancement of AI Output - Transparency (Prompt + AI Use Declaration) - Effective and Ethical AI Usage To be selected to the Final Presentation, each student needs: * All on-going assessments (Evaluation 1 & Evaluation 2) >=5/10 * No cheating during the project progress
